objectives.understand: Why a fixed weekly routine and built-in checks keep an agent useful over time.
objectives.do: Set a weekly trigger and run your agent on fresh material with the quality checks.
objectives.demonstrate: Plan a realistic routine, check agent output properly and share your work honestly.
objectives.apply: Submit your agent file and Playbook, and complete the share step with one person who needs it.

discover.title: Mission briefing: make it stick
discover.scenario: An agent that ran once is a good day's work. Kemi, an HR officer in Abeokuta, built hers on Tuesday, used it on Wednesday and had forgotten it by the next Monday. What she needed was a reminder, a ten-minute weekly review and one colleague who saw what it could do. Today you set up yours to last.

keyIdeas: A routine is which day, which time and which job, set as a repeating reminder. You start each run yourself.
Check every run with the four questions, and once a week fix one weak instruction in the agent file.
Share honestly: one real output, one person who needs it, no pressure tactics.

missions.title: Set a routine that survives
missions.prompt: Which routine is most likely to keep Kemi's agent running every week?

options.feedback: That is how agents get forgotten. The routine needs a fixed day and time.

options.text: A repeating Friday 3pm reminder to run the weekly staff-update agent, because that's when the update is due.
options.feedback: Yes. Which day, which time, which job, tied to when the work is due.

options.text: Run it every hour so it never falls behind.
options.feedback: More runs are not better. Each run needs fresh material and your check.

options.text: Wait until a paid app can schedule it automatically.
options.feedback: Not needed. The reminder is the trigger, and it is free.

missions.hint: The lesson asks you to decide three things in writing.
missions.support: A routine survives when it is attached to a moment that already exists in your week. When is Kemi's update due?
missions.explain: A fixed reminder at the moment the job comes due, for one specific agent, is simple enough to keep, and that is why it works.

missions.title: Share it the right way
missions.scenario: Kemi is proud of the staff update her agent produced and wants to show others.
missions.prompt: Which actions match the share challenge? Select all that apply.

options.text: Show one colleague who struggles with weekly reports the actual output.
options.feedback: Yes. One real output to one person who needs the skill.

options.text: Point them to the free Day 1 lesson, which takes about 10 minutes.
options.feedback: Yes. Let them try it for themselves.

options.text: Log in her Playbook whom she showed and what happened.
options.feedback: Yes. The log is part of the step.

options.text: Forward a sales message to every WhatsApp group she's in.
options.feedback: No. Mass messages read as spam, and the course deliberately avoids them.

options.text: Tell her colleague the course guarantees a promotion.
options.feedback: No. The course makes no promises about income or jobs.

missions.hint: One output, one person, one honest demonstration, and a log.
missions.support: People share what made them look competent. Which options show the real work to someone who needs it, without pressure or promises?
missions.explain: A cleaner report in a colleague's hand speaks for itself. Leaving out scripts, pressure and promises keeps a recommendation trustworthy.

advanced.title: Advanced: quality control at scale
advanced.scenario: Kemi's agent draft says: 'Six staff completed training (₦240,000 total). Leave roster approved by the MD. Next training: 14 November.'
advanced.prompt: Sort each item by what Kemi should do with it before using the draft.
categories: Remove unless she can confirm it

items.feedback: A count to check against the attendance register.
A figure to check against receipts. Numbers always get verified.

items.text: Leave roster approved by the MD
items.feedback: An approval her notes didn't mention. Remove it unless she can confirm it happened.

items.text: The agent keeps adding approvals that aren't in the notes
items.feedback: A repeated pattern means a weak instruction. Add a rule: 'Never state an approval unless it is in my notes.'

advanced.hint: Facts get checked, unsupported claims get removed, and repeated problems get fixed at the source.
advanced.support: One-off details are fixed in the draft. A problem that keeps coming back is fixed in the agent file, so next week's run is better.
advanced.explain: Verify the numbers, cut what you can't confirm, and fix one weak instruction per week. An agent improves only as fast as its instructions do.
